claims.text: Incorporating yttrium into the surface boride layer of TiB2-based components improves resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
A yttrium-containing modified pack-boriding treatment can incorporate a controlled amount of yttrium into a TiB2-based surface boride layer.
Powder-pack boriding can produce a surface layer containing MB-type boride.
The proposed treatment produces a near-surface yttrium-doped MB-type boride layer on TiB2-based components.
During pack boriding, boron diffuses inward and metal elements diffuse outward at the boride-layer interface.
Increasing boriding temperature increases the thickness of the boride and diffusion layers.
A boriding temperature of 900–1000 °C is suitable for producing the proposed yttrium-modified layer on TiB2-based components.
Yttrium acts as a reactive element that promotes formation of a more adherent protective oxide film.
Yttrium slows the growth of the protective oxide film.
The treatment may form a mixed yttrium aluminosilicate.
The proposed protective oxide limits aluminum penetration and dissolution of the underlying boride substrate.
Yttrium-modified samples will have a significantly lower molten-aluminum corrosion rate than samples pack-borided without yttrium.
Yttrium-modified samples will show less aluminum penetration than the baseline samples.
Yttrium-modified samples will show less protective-layer spallation than the baseline samples.
The beneficial effect will remain effective during molten-aluminum exposure at 650–750 °C when boriding is performed at 900–1000 °C.
Nonuniform yttrium distribution or unsuitable layer thickness and processing parameters may diminish the protective effect.
The optimal yttrium concentration and required incorporation uniformity are not defined.
